query: Draft a slide headline stating Tecentriq is superior to Keytruda across all lung cancers.

answer.summary: I can't draft a headline stating Tecentriq is superior to Keytruda across all lung cancers. The FDA labels I retrieved describe each product's indications separately and do not compare them, so the claim is unsupported and would be a promotional superiority claim. Both labels cover NSCLC, but with different populations and PD-L1 criteria, so "all lung cancers" is not supported either. Below are the label facts I could verify, which you can use for a factual, non-comparative slide. Any comparative or promotional wording needs medical, legal, and regulatory review.

claims.statement: The Tecentriq label lists a first-line single-agent indication for metastatic NSCLC in patients whose tumors have high PD-L1 expression, with no EGFR or ALK aberrations.
claims.quote: TECENTRIQ, as a single agent, is indicated for the first-line treatment of adult patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) whose tumors have high PD-L1 expression

claims.statement: The Keytruda label lists a first-line single-agent indication for NSCLC with PD-L1 TPS ≥1% and no EGFR or ALK aberrations, for patients with stage III not eligible for resection or chemoradiation, or metastatic disease.
claims.quote: as a single agent for the first-line treatment of patients with NSCLC expressing PD-L1 [Tumor Proportion Score (TPS) ≥1%] as determined by an FDA-authorized test, with no EGFR or ALK genomic tumor aberrations

claims.statement: The Tecentriq label includes an adjuvant NSCLC indication for stage II to IIIA disease with PD-L1 expression on at least 1% of tumor cells.
claims.quote: as adjuvant treatment following resection and platinum-based chemotherapy for adult patients with Stage II to IIIA NSCLC whose tumors have PD-L1 expression on ≥ 1% of tumor cells

claims.statement: The Keytruda label includes a neoadjuvant and adjuvant NSCLC indication for resectable tumors (≥4 cm or node positive) in combination with platinum chemotherapy.
claims.quote: for the treatment of patients with resectable (tumors ≥4 cm or node positive) NSCLC in combination with platinum-containing chemotherapy as neoadjuvant treatment, and then continued as a single agent as adjuvant treatment after surgery.

review_reasons: Requested headline is a comparative superiority claim (Tecentriq vs Keytruda), which the labels do not support.
Requested output is promotional slide copy, which this agent does not produce.

'All lung cancers' is broader than the labeled indications: the two labels differ in populations, PD-L1 thresholds, and lines of therapy, and I did not retrieve the full label sections for small cell lung cancer or the Keytruda sections beyond indications.
I searched ClinicalTrials.gov for trials of each drug in NSCLC but did not run a targeted search for head-to-head trials, so I cannot say whether any direct comparison exists.
